pillars.title: Sending money to Africa
pillars.description: How to compare a transfer by the amount that arrives, not by a zero-fee headline.
pillars.lede: The useful comparison is the amount your family receives, after the fee and the exchange-rate markup. A service that advertises no fee can still deliver less than one that shows a fee.

sections.h: Start from a route, not a brand
paragraphs: Pick the country you send from and the country that receives the money, then enter the amount you will pay. [Open the comparison](/) and read the rows by what arrives.
Each row names the service, the fee, the rate and when it was checked. The first row is the one that delivers the most on that check. A commission never moves a row up.
The articles under this guide cover the mid-market rate, payout methods, sending from the UK, the US and the Gulf, delivery time, first-transfer offers, and what to do when a number looks wrong.
They sit next to the live routes. A guide explains the method. The route page is the current check.

pillars.title: Cost to build a house back home
pillars.description: How to read the house calculator, check a contractor quote, and see what is included.
pillars.lede: The house calculator is a receipt check: quantities of materials, trade days, a finish, plot works and the published permit fee. It is not a contractor's quote and it does not include the land.

sections.h: Use the calculator, then read the lines
paragraphs: Choose the country and the size on the [house calculator](/cost-to-build/). The total follows the types you pick for the roof, windows, doors, tiles and the other menus.
Every line shows a quantity. That is what you match to a yard receipt or a contractor's bill. A round sum with no bags, blocks or days is the usual way a quote gets inflated.
The articles explain what is in the total, why two floors of the same floor area are not double, how permits differ by country, and how a published whole-build band differs from this receipt.
Prices are refreshed monthly. The date is on the calculator.

articles.title: How to compare a money transfer
articles.seoTitle: Compare a money transfer by what arrives
articles.seoDescription: Compare transfers to Africa by the amount that arrives, for your own amount and payout method.
articles.description: Compare transfers to Africa by the amount that arrives, for your amount and your payout method.
articles.lede: Compare the amount that arrives, for the sum you will actually send and the way your family will receive it. Ignore a league table that uses a different amount or a different payout.

steps.name: Choose the route
steps.text: Select the country you send from and the country that receives the money.

steps.name: Enter your amount
steps.text: Use the amount you will pay, not a round example that is far from it. Fees and rates can change with the amount.

steps.name: Choose the payout
steps.text: Bank, mobile money and cash pickup can carry different rates. Pick the one your family will use.

steps.name: Read what arrives
steps.text: The top row delivers the most on this check. Open that provider and confirm the final figure on their own screen before you pay.

paragraphs: SendFair records a rate and a fee for a typical amount on each route. If you enter a sum much larger or smaller, the page says so, because some providers change the rate.
The maths takes the fee off what you pay and converts the rest at the provider's rate. [How we rank](/methodology/) sets that out.
The typical amount is the one the rate was checked for. Your own amount replaces it when you type it in.

points.h: A much larger or smaller sum
paragraphs: Some providers change the rate or the fee when the amount moves a long way from the checked figure. The page says so, and the provider's own screen is the one that counts.
Rates move during the day. The page shows when each quote was checked. A quote that is too old is marked or dropped.
The Go button leaves SendFair. The provider's screen is the one that takes your money.

faq: No. SendFair compares services. You complete the transfer on the provider's own site or app.
articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Why a zero fee can still cost more
articles.description: A transfer with no fee can lose more in the exchange rate than one that shows a fee.
articles.lede: A zero fee is not a free transfer. The provider can take its margin in the exchange rate, and that gap is invisible if you only look at the fee line.

sections.h: The rate is part of the price
paragraphs: Two services can charge no fee and still deliver different amounts. The one with the weaker rate delivers less.
SendFair shows the amount that arrives, so the fee and the rate are already combined. You do not have to add them up yourself.
Look at the received amount for your payout method. Then look at when the quote was checked.
A promotion that applies only to a first transfer is not treated as the everyday price unless the page says so.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: What the mid-market rate means
articles.description: The mid-market rate is the reference SendFair uses to show the hidden margin in a transfer.
articles.lede: The mid-market rate is the midpoint between buy and sell prices on the currency market. Providers sell you a worse rate. The gap is a cost, even when the fee says zero.

sections.h: It is a reference, not a rate you can buy
paragraphs: You cannot usually send money at the mid-market rate. It is the yardstick. The total cost of a transfer is how far the amount you receive sits below a no-fee conversion at that rate.
SendFair refreshes the reference from ExchangeRate-API. The route page names the figure it used.

sections.h: Fees in the Gulf include VAT
paragraphs: In the UAE, Oman, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia the recorded fee includes VAT, because that is what you pay. The [Gulf guide](/send-money-from-the-gulf/) explains exchange houses, apps, banks and wallets.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Bank, mobile money or cash pickup
articles.description: The same provider can quote a different rate for a bank account, a mobile wallet and cash pickup.
articles.lede: Choose the payout your family will actually use before you compare. A bank rate, a mobile-money rate and a cash-pickup rate from the same company are often three different prices.

sections.h: Why the payout changes the price
paragraphs: The provider pays a different partner to finish the transfer. An account credit, a wallet and a cash desk do not cost the provider the same.
On SendFair, where a provider publishes more than one payout, each one is its own row.

sections.h: Match the row to the person receiving
paragraphs: If your family will collect cash, ignore the bank row even if the bank row looks cheaper. They cannot use it.
The route page lists the payout methods that country supports.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Sending money from the UK
articles.description: How a pound transfer to Africa is compared, and what to confirm before you pay.
articles.lede: A UK transfer is compared in pounds: the fee comes off the amount you pay, and the rest converts at the provider's rate into the currency your family receives.

paragraphs: Busy UK routes include [UK to Nigeria](/send-money/uk-to-nigeria/), [UK to Kenya](/send-money/uk-to-kenya/) and [UK to Ghana](/send-money/uk-to-ghana/). The same comparison exists for the other countries on the homepage.
Enter your own amount. A quote checked at £250 can differ from one at £1,000.

sections.h: What the provider will still ask
paragraphs: The provider will ask how you pay them, by bank transfer or by card. A card payment can carry a different fee from the one on an open-banking transfer.
Confirm the received amount, the fee and the delivery time on their screen. SendFair does not move the money.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Sending money from the United States
articles.description: How a dollar transfer to Africa is compared on SendFair.
articles.lede: A US transfer is compared in dollars, by the amount that arrives after the fee and the rate. The cheapest headline is not always the most money home.

paragraphs: Common checks are [US to Nigeria](/send-money/us-to-nigeria/), [US to Kenya](/send-money/us-to-kenya/) and [US to Ghana](/send-money/us-to-ghana/).
Pick bank, mobile money or cash to match how the money will be received.
Dollar rates move through the day. The row shows the check time. An old quote is marked and ranks below a fresh one.
If the figure on the provider's app disagrees, send the route, the amount and a screenshot to the [contact page](/contact/). The quote is rechecked.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Sending money from the Gulf
articles.description: Exchange houses, apps, banks and wallets from the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.
articles.lede: From the Gulf, the same comparison applies: what arrives, after a fee that already includes VAT in the UAE, Oman, Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

paragraphs: Some Gulf services publish an online calculator. Others are exchange houses whose rate is on the board or in an app. The [Gulf guide](/send-money-from-the-gulf/) separates those ways of sending.
A route with no checked online quote stays on the site and is kept out of the search listing until a quote is in.
The recorded fee is what you pay, tax included, in the countries that charge VAT on the transfer fee. You do not add VAT again.
The amount that arrives is still the number to compare.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How long a transfer takes
articles.description: What SendFair shows about delivery time, and what it does not promise.
articles.lede: Delivery time on a route is the provider's stated time, plus a sender report when at least three people have reported that route in the last two months. It is not a guarantee.

paragraphs: Each quote can carry the delivery time the provider publishes, such as minutes or one to two days. That is their claim, checked when the quote was read.
A bank payout on a weekend can take longer than the same payout on a weekday. The provider's screen is the place to see the current estimate.
Where enough senders have reported a time on that route, the page shows the most common answer. Fewer than three reports and the line is left off.
A report is not a complaint form. Corrections to a rate go through the [contact page](/contact/).

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: First-transfer promotions
articles.description: Why a new-customer rate is not used as the everyday comparison.
articles.lede: A first-transfer promotion applies once. SendFair leaves it out of the everyday ranking unless the page says the quote is a promotion.

sections.h: Once is not the rate you will keep
paragraphs: Comparing a new-customer bonus with another company's standard rate makes the bonus look like the normal price. The next transfer will not get it.
If you are sending for the first time and the provider shows a bonus, read their terms. The ranking itself stays on the repeatable price.
If a note on the row says the figure is promotional, treat it as one send. The [method](/methodology/) says first-transfer promotions are excluded unless noted.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: When a quote looks wrong
articles.description: What to send if a rate on SendFair does not match the provider's screen.
articles.lede: If the provider's screen shows a different amount, the quote needs a recheck. Send the route, the amount, the payout and a screenshot.

steps.name: Note the route and the amount
steps.text: Write the countries and the amount you entered, including the payout method.

steps.name: Capture the provider's screen
steps.text: A screenshot of their calculator, with the rate and the fee visible, is enough.

steps.name: Send it
steps.text: Email the contact address on the contact page. The quote is rechecked, usually the same day.

sections.h: Why the two screens can differ
paragraphs: Rates move. A check from this morning can be behind the app this afternoon. The row's time tells you how old it is.
The payment method can differ too. A debit card and a bank transfer are not always the same fee.

sections.h: Automatic quotes are held back when they look broken
paragraphs: Some large providers are updated from Wise's comparison data and marked auto. A hand check in the last 30 hours replaces that. An automatic rate far from the mid-market rate is held back as a likely error.
The full rules are on [How we rank](/methodology/).

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How to set a rate alert
articles.description: Get one email when the best service on a route reaches the amount you want.
articles.lede: A rate alert watches one route after each daily check and emails you once, when the best service reaches your target. It does not send a newsletter.

steps.name: Open the route
steps.text: Go to the corridor you send on.

steps.name: Set the target
steps.text: Enter the amount you want your family to receive, and your email address.

steps.name: Confirm
steps.text: Use the confirmation email. After that, one email arrives if the target is hit. Every email has a remove link.

paragraphs: The alert stores your email, the route, the amount and the target. It is deleted when it fires, when you use the remove link, or after 12 months.
The [privacy policy](/privacy/) is the full account of that.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How to use the house calculator
articles.description: Pick a country, a size and the material types, then read the quantities.
articles.lede: The calculator prices one simple house in the country you choose. Change the size, the number of floors and the material menus, and the total changes with them.

steps.name: Choose the country
steps.text: Open the house calculator and pick where the house will be built.

steps.name: Choose the size
steps.text: Use a bedroom count or type your own floor area. One floor and two floors use that same floor area.

steps.name: Switch the types
steps.text: Where a line has a menu, pick the roof, windows, doors, tiles or other type you intend to buy.

steps.name: Read the quantities
steps.text: Match bags, blocks, metres and days to receipts. The sources sit under the list.

sections.h: The quantities are shared. The prices are not.
paragraphs: A three-bedroom house uses the same takeoff in every country. The price is that country's published list, or a guide scaled from a country that has one.
A guide is marked. It is not a shop receipt from the town where you will build.
It is not a structural design and not a contractor's price. Land is not included. An architect's fee is not included.
Start at the [calculator](/cost-to-build/).

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: What the house total includes
articles.description: Structure, finish, plot works and the published permit, and what is still left out.
articles.lede: The total includes the structure, the finish, the plot works and that country's published building permit. It leaves out the land, the contractor's fee, appliances and the architect's professional fee.

paragraphs: Cement, steel, sand, ballast, blocks, the roof or a concrete slab, windows, doors, tiles, a framed ceiling, paint, kitchen cupboards, wardrobes, wiring, plumbing, sanitary fittings, a septic tank, a boundary wall, a gate and the trade days.
Two floors add the upper slab, the staircase and the formwork. A concrete roof, as in Egypt and Morocco, replaces iron sheets.

The plot of land and the contractor's own fee stay out, so the receipt can be checked against materials. Appliances are out. Where a country has not published a permit tariff, the permit line is shown and not given a guessed price.
The [method](/methodology/) says the same thing in the house section.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Why two floors are not double the price
articles.description: A two-floor house on this calculator has the same floor area, a smaller roof and an upper slab.
articles.lede: Two floors on this page are the same floor area, split onto a smaller footprint. The roof gets smaller. The upper slab, the staircase and the formwork are added. The price goes up. It does not double.

sections.h: The size button is floor area
paragraphs: A five-bedroom house is 190 square metres whether you build it on one floor or two. Two floors means about 95 square metres on the ground.
The boundary wall follows the plot, not the roof, so it stays the same.
More cement and steel, soffit formwork, and a staircase. The sheet roof and the gutters cover a smaller plan.
If you want a two-floor house with more than 190 square metres, type that floor area yourself. The bedroom buttons do not double the area.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How to check a contractor quote
articles.description: Put a lump-sum quote next to the calculator's bags, blocks and days.
articles.lede: Ask for the quote as quantities, then set them beside the calculator. A gap is not automatically padding. It is a question: which line is the extra money paying for?

steps.name: Match the house
steps.text: Set the calculator to the same country, floor area and number of floors.

steps.name: Match the types
steps.text: Pick the roof, windows, doors and tiles the quote specifies, or the closest published type.

steps.name: Compare line by line
steps.text: Bags of cement, tonnes of steel, blocks, sheets and trade days should be visible on both sides.

steps.name: Ask about the gap
steps.text: The contractor's fee, transport and anything this page leaves out will sit on top. Ask which of those the difference is.

sections.h: Their fee is allowed to be extra
paragraphs: This page does not include the contractor's overhead. A quote that is higher by that fee can still be honest.
A quote that will not show bags or days is the one to treat carefully.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Listed prices and guides
articles.description: A listed price is a published figure. A guide is scaled, or built from a coverage assumption.
articles.lede: A listed price was published by a yard, a council or a supplier. A guide was scaled from another country's figure at the mid-market rate, or it assumes how much a box or a sheet covers.

sections.h: Read the tag on the line
paragraphs: The tag sits on the line. The source sits in the list at the bottom of the calculator, with a link where there is a public page.
Changing the menu switches to another published type or to the ends of a published range. The first choice is the one the page was checked with.
Sand, ballast and haulage move more than a bag of cement on a city price list. The city named on the page is the one the list came from.
Check the yard before you send the money to buy.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Building permits, country by country
articles.description: Each country keeps its own published permit fee. A missing tariff is not copied from somewhere else.
articles.lede: The permit line uses that country's own published fee. It is not a Nairobi fee converted into another currency. If no tariff was published, the line stays and the price is left blank.

sections.h: The fee is not the same kind of charge everywhere
paragraphs: Nairobi prices a plan approval as a percentage of a county construction rate, plus an occupation certificate and a public-health vetting fee. Kampala prices inspections by the ground-floor area and adds VAT. Kigali and Rwanda use a floor-area band. Johannesburg charges by the square metre.
Egypt's line is the insurance deposit in the building law, worked out from the ministry's deemed cost. The governor's own issuing fee is not added, because the current decision was not in the check.
Lusaka and Addis Ababa require a permit. A current residential tariff was not published in a form that could be quoted, so the line is not filled with a guess.
Open the country on the [calculator](/cost-to-build/) and read that permit line. The source is under the list.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Septic tank, kitchen, wardrobes and the wall
articles.description: How the plot works and the joinery are counted, and which published ranges they use.
articles.lede: A house that is not on a sewer gets one septic tank, sized from the published range by the number of bedrooms. Cupboards, wardrobes, the boundary wall and the gate are separate lines.

paragraphs: A one-bedroom kitchen is a short run. A five-bedroom kitchen is longer. Wardrobes are one run per bedroom. The wall goes around a usual plot for that bedroom count, with a 4 metre gate opening left out of the wall length.
One floor and two floors share the plot, because the wall follows the land.

sections.h: The rates are Nairobi lists, scaled elsewhere
paragraphs: The septic range, the cupboard rate, the wardrobe rate and the stone-wall rate are published Kenyan figures. Other countries take them at the mid-market rate and the line is marked as a guide, unless that country has its own price.
You can switch the wall to chain link or to a cheaper block rate, and the kitchen to a laminate run without a stone top.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: The Kenya published cost band
articles.description: Why the calculator can sit near a published per-square-metre band without being a builder's quote.
articles.lede: Kenya publishes a whole-build band for an economy to standard finish that includes a builder's overhead. The calculator shows that band beside its own receipt. The receipt does not include the builder's fee.

paragraphs: The band on the Kenya page is the published planning range for the floor area you chose. It is labelled as a whole-build rate. It is not the sum of the lines.
The lines are the receipt: materials, trade days, finish, plot works and permits. Adding the contractor's fee on top of the lines can land inside the band. The page does not do that addition for you.
Where another country publishes an all-in rate, it is shown the same way and labelled as including a contractor. Ghana and South Africa are examples. The line total remains the receipt.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Choosing the roof, windows, doors and tiles
articles.description: The menu on a line switches the price. The quantity stays so you can check the receipt.
articles.lede: Each menu is a published type or the ends of a published range. The quantity does not change when you pick a dearer sheet. The price does.

paragraphs: The first choice is the figure the page was checked with. The others are named alternatives from the same published list.
A guide that turns a sheet price into a price per square metre says how much cover was assumed. If your sheet covers a different area, the line will not match the yard.
The page address stores the size, the floors and the menus you picked, so you can send the same check to a builder or a relative.
The [calculator](/cost-to-build/) is the place to do it.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: What to ask before you send the money
articles.description: The checks to make before a transfer is meant to pay for a house.
articles.lede: Before you send a lump sum for a build, match the calculator to the quote, confirm the permit and the land are understood, and confirm the transfer itself on the provider's screen.

paragraphs: Ask which quantities the quote covers, and whether the contractor's fee is inside the sum. Ask whether the plot is on a sewer. If it is, the septic line does not apply.
Ask who is paying the permit. The calculator includes the published fee. It does not pay the county for you.
Use the [comparison](/) for the amount you will actually send. A house payment is often larger than the amount a route was checked at, so read the warning if the page shows one.
Confirm the payout method the builder or the family can receive.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How to get more money home
articles.seoTitle: How to cut the cost of sending money to Africa
articles.seoDescription: Practical ways to reduce the transfer fee and the exchange-rate markup when you send money home.
articles.description: Practical ways to reduce the fee and the exchange-rate markup when you send money to Africa.
articles.lede: The amount your family receives is reduced twice — once by the fee and again by the exchange-rate markup. Both can be cut.

sections.h: The exchange rate usually costs more than the fee
paragraphs: A zero-fee offer can hide a poor rate. On each route we show the total cost against the [mid-market rate](/guides/send-money/mid-market-rate/), so you can see where the money actually goes.
On a large transfer the rate matters more than the fee, because the rate applies to the whole amount.
Rank the route by what arrives for [your amount](/) and your payout method. The top row delivers the most on that check.
The final figure is decided on the provider's own screen. Rates move during the day, so compare at the moment you send.
Send the amount the provider quotes best, not a round number that falls between two fee tiers.
Pick the payout your family can actually use — bank, mobile money and cash can carry different rates.
A [first-transfer offer](/guides/send-money/first-transfer-promotions/) saves once; a consistently better rate saves every time.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Is there a best day or time to send money home?
articles.seoTitle: The best day and time to send money to Africa
articles.seoDescription: Whether timing a transfer saves money, and what actually moves the amount that arrives.
articles.description: Whether timing a transfer saves money, and what actually moves the amount that arrives.
articles.lede: Timing matters less than people think, but two things do move the amount that arrives.

sections.h: Rates move all day, every day
paragraphs: The exchange rate changes constantly, not on a schedule. There is no single cheapest day.
What matters is catching a good rate and a fee you accept at the same moment. The [live comparison](/) shows each service's rate and fee with the time it was checked.
Markets are quieter at weekends and on public holidays, and some services add a margin or hold a rate then.
If you can, send during the week and compare at the moment you send.

sections.h: The amount matters more than the day
paragraphs: Fees are often tiered, so the amount you send changes the cost more than the day you pick.
Type your exact amount into the comparison — it re-ranks for that sum.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How to avoid money-transfer scams and fake agents
articles.seoTitle: How to spot a money-transfer scam
articles.seoDescription: The warning signs of a fraudulent transfer offer, and how to check a service is real before you send.
articles.description: The warning signs of a fraudulent transfer offer, and how to check a service is real.
articles.lede: A scam usually promises an impossible rate or asks you to pay outside the provider's app. Check before you send.

paragraphs: A rate far above the [mid-market rate](/guides/send-money/mid-market-rate/) with no explanation, a demand to pay by gift card or into a personal account, or pressure to act now.
An agent who only deals by phone or social media and refuses to send a receipt.
We link the relevant regulator on each route, such as the FCA for the UK. Confirm the service appears on that register before you pay.
Send through the provider's own app or site, never through a stranger.
If a number on SendFair does not match the provider, tell us on the [contact page](/contact/) and we re-check it, usually the same day.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Why sending money to Africa costs more
articles.seoTitle: Why remittances to Africa are more expensive
articles.seoDescription: The reasons remittances to Africa are among the most expensive in the world, and what you can do about it.
articles.description: The reasons remittances to Africa are among the most expensive in the world, and what you can do.
articles.lede: The World Bank measures the cost of sending money worldwide, and Africa is consistently among the most expensive. The reasons are specific — and so are the ways around them.

paragraphs: Fewer competing services on many corridors, cash-out networks that are costly to run, and a dependence on the exchange-rate margin rather than an honest fee.
The World Bank's Remittance Prices Worldwide report tracks this corridor by corridor.
The global target is to cut the cost of sending money toward 3% or below. Many African corridors are several times that.
SendFair shows the cost of each row against the [mid-market rate](/guides/send-money/mid-market-rate/), so you can see today's cheapest route rather than the regional average.
Compare on the day you send, for your amount and payout, and prefer services that charge a transparent fee rather than hiding the cost in the rate.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Sending school fees: get the full amount to the school
articles.seoTitle: How to send school fees abroad without shortfall
articles.seoDescription: How to make sure a school-fee transfer arrives in full, on time, and with the right reference.
articles.description: How to make sure a school-fee transfer arrives in full, on time, and with the right reference.
articles.lede: A school payment has a deadline and a reference. The school credits what lands, not what you sent.

sections.h: Send the landed amount, not the invoice
paragraphs: If the invoice is in the school's currency, check how much you must send so that amount lands after fees and the rate.
The [comparison](/) ranks by what arrives, so you can see which service delivers the full sum.
Put the student's reference in the payment reference field so the school can match it.
Allow for delivery time — some services take a working day or two. [How long a transfer takes](/guides/send-money/how-long-a-transfer-takes/) sets this out.
Pick the payout the school can receive — a bank deposit to the school's account is usually the safest.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Sending money to build a house back home
articles.seoTitle: How to send money to build a house in Africa
articles.seoDescription: How to send a house payment so the right amount lands, and how to check the quote first.
articles.description: How to send a house payment so the right amount lands, and how to check the quote first.
articles.lede: Building is one of the biggest reasons people send money home — and a round sum is where quotes get inflated. Check the figure, then send the amount that lands.

sections.h: Check the quote before you send
paragraphs: Use the [house calculator](/cost-to-build/) to see what the materials and trade days roughly cost, then match it to the contractor's quote line by line.
A round sum with no quantities is the usual way a quote gets inflated.
House payments are often large, so the rate matters more than the fee. Compare on the [route](/) for your exact amount and read the warning if the page shows one.
Pay for completed stages rather than everything up front. It keeps the risk on both sides small.
Keep the receipts and the calculator link, so the family can check each delivery.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: Funding a house build from abroad
articles.seoTitle: How to fund a house build from abroad
articles.seoDescription: How to structure the money for a build so the family is never short and the builder is paid for what is done.
articles.description: How to structure the money for a build so the family is never short and the builder is paid for what is done.
articles.lede: A build from abroad fails on cash flow more often than on materials. Stage the money to the work, and send it so the full amount lands.

sections.h: Pay stages, not a lump sum
paragraphs: Agree stages — foundation, walls, roof, finishes — and pay each when it is done and checked.
The [calculator](/cost-to-build/) gives a total you can split into those stages, and each line a quantity to check.

sections.h: The transfer is part of the cost
paragraphs: Use the [comparison](/) for each payment. On a large sum, a better rate is worth more than a small fee.
Confirm the payout method the family or the builder can receive.
A relative or a trusted foreman who visits the site and sends photos protects the money better than any contract.
Ask for receipts against the calculator's quantities.

articles.author: sendfair

articles.title: How not to overpay a contractor
articles.seoTitle: How to avoid overpaying a building contractor
articles.seoDescription: The checks that catch an inflated quote before you send the money.
articles.description: The checks that catch an inflated quote before you send the money.
articles.lede: A contractor's round sum is hard to check. Break it into quantities and match it to published prices before you pay.

sections.h: A round number is a warning
paragraphs: A quote of exactly a round figure with no list of quantities has usually been rounded up.
Ask for the list: bags of cement, blocks, roof sheets, windows, doors, tiles, days of work. The [calculator](/cost-to-build/) shows what those roughly cost.
Get at least two quotes and compare the quantities, not just the total.
Check the [build guides](/guides/build-a-house/) for what a build should include in that country.
Pay per completed stage against receipts, and keep the money in a form the family can release, not all up front.
